ai_reasoning: The task measures the face inversion effect for sexualized targets, which is a perceptual measure rather than an episodic-memory outcome.
Mild AD dementia, active tDCS vs sham, randomised. MMSE is the primary outcome; check the full text for a word-recall secondary outcome.
A systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary trial.
AD patients randomised to 40 Hz tACS vs sham. Reports the ADAS-Cog memory score; check that the patients have mild AD.
Healthy adults, theta tACS vs sham sessions, with free recall and temporal-order memory outcomes.
tDCS vs sham during the Cambridge Face Memory Test, which tests recognition of learned faces. Check whether this counts as an episodic-memory outcome and that a sham group exists.
Fear-extinction recall measured by skin conductance, not an episodic-memory test.
Healthy older adults, tACS vs sham crossover, with a temporal-order (episodic sequence) memory task.

PACt-MD moderator analysis: tDCS+CR vs sham, verbal memory outcome. The sample mixes remitted depression with MCI, and this is a secondary analysis, so prefer the main trial report and check for MCI-only data.
A study protocol with no results.
Dysphoric participants selected on depressive symptoms (BDI-II > 13), an ineligible group; the memory tasks are bias measures.
Healthy young adults randomised to gamma tACS or sham, with verbal recognition (d-prime) as the primary outcome.
Healthy adults randomised to PPC tACS or sham after learning, with word-recognition outcomes.
Healthy adults randomised to parietal theta tACS or sham, with a face-scene associative memory task.
Healthy adults, theta tACS vs sham during retrieval, with picture-recognition accuracy.
Mild AD, theta tACS vs sham, randomised. Memory is reported only as the MMSE recall item here; check the full text for an eligible memory test.
Older women with subjective decline or normal cognition, tDCS vs sham. The memory outcome is the ACE-R memory domain; check whether it qualifies.
Healthy adults randomised to bifrontal tACS or sham. Working memory is primary, but an episodic-memory accuracy outcome is also reported.
MCI patients, multi-site or single-site tACS vs sham, with a recognition-memory outcome.
Prodromal and mild AD, randomised gamma tACS vs sham. Check the full text for an episodic-memory measure among the efficacy end points.
A rat study.
tACS (theta, gamma) vs sham during a source-memory task. Same title as pmid:38854074, so possibly a duplicate record.
tACS (3 Hz, 8 Hz) vs sham during encoding, with a temporal-memory outcome.
Non-demented older adults randomised to theta-gamma tACS or sham with cognitive training, with episodic-memory outcomes (story recall).
Substance use disorder, an ineligible clinical group, with emotion-regulation outcomes.
Dementia patients, 40 Hz tACS vs sham crossover. Check the dementia type and severity and whether an episodic-memory score is reported.
Bipolar depression, open-label single arm with no sham.
Prospective memory within a working-memory task, not an eligible episodic-memory outcome.
Memory for newly learned immunology concepts, framed and tested as semantic knowledge.
Schizophrenia, an ineligible clinical group.
Healthy adults randomised to gamma tACS or sham, with word-pair cued recall.
Healthy young adults randomised to anodal tDCS or sham, with associative and item memory outcomes.

AD dementia, HD-tDCS vs sham, randomised, with RAVLT learning and delayed recall as primary outcome. Check that severity is mild.
Healthy adults, HD theta-otDCS vs sham crossover, with face-word and object-location associative memory.
Younger and older adults randomised to tDCS or sham before episodic retrieval tasks.
Novel word acquisition (fast mapping) measured as lexical learning; check if a recognition test of the studied words is reported.
A systematic review and meta-analysis in depression.
Emotional prosody recognition, not episodic memory.
MCI, anodal tDCS vs placebo tDCS with VR cognitive training, with episodic-memory outcomes.
tACS vs sham during a source-memory task. Same title as pmid:40800986, so possibly a duplicate record.
HD-tDCS vs sham during a proverb-name associative recognition task.
Novel-word learning with focal tDCS vs sham; the outcome is word-learning success. Check if it is a recall test of studied items.
MCI, home tDCS vs sham, with a visual recognition task and MMSE. Check whether the recognition task is an episodic-memory test.
Primary progressive aphasia, an ineligible group, with short-term and working memory outcomes.
A study protocol with no results.
A rat study.
Working memory outcomes only.
Pooled reanalysis of earlier tDCS vs sham studies in older adults with verbal recall. The samples overlap the original trials, so prefer those.
tACS (theta, beta) vs sham after learning, with free recall outcomes.
Healthy adults randomised to anodal or sham tDCS during cued recall of a video.
Patients with cognitive impairment randomised to tDCS or sham with training; a verbal learning and memory test is a secondary outcome. Check the diagnostic criteria.
Amyloid-positive AD, home tDCS vs sham, randomised, with verbal memory tests. Check severity and group sizes (8 per arm).
AD patients randomised to tDCS or sham, with ADAS-Cog word recall. Check that severity is mild.
AD/MCI and controls, tDCS vs sham crossover, during virtual place learning. Spatial navigation recall may not count as an eligible episodic-memory outcome.
Early AD, home tDCS vs sham, randomised, with immediate and delayed recall. May share patients with pmid:36660288.
Anodal, cathodal or sham tDCS before the Cambridge Face Memory Test. Same question as other CFMT studies: does face-identity memory count as episodic memory?
All patients received active tDCS; the randomised comparison is benzoate vs placebo drug, so there is no sham tDCS arm.
Healthy adults, remotely supervised tDCS (left, right) vs sham, with an episodic recognition task.
Schizophrenia, an ineligible clinical group.
Face perception (featural and holistic recognition) tasks, not episodic memory.
MCI, Tai Chi or walking with tDCS vs sham tDCS, randomised, with a memory outcome. Check which memory test is used.
Phonological working memory (nonword repetition) only.
Healthy young adults, tDCS vs sham during encoding, with recognition and free recall.
Healthy adults, HD-tDCS over left VLPFC, with free recall of value-weighted word lists. Check that one group received sham in the second session.

Children with dyslexia, an ineligible group.

Emotional prosody recognition, not episodic memory.

Early AD, gamma tACS vs sham crossover, with RAVLT and face-name association outcomes.
A study protocol with no results.
Healthy adults, anodal, cathodal or sham tDCS while memorising face-name-profession pairs, with later recall.
AD, multisite tDCS vs sham with cognitive stimulation, randomised. ADAS-Cog is reported as a total; check for the word-recall score.
Current applied to the occipital nerve to target the locus coeruleus, which is peripheral nerve stimulation rather than transcranial tDCS/tACS.
Healthy adults randomised to left or right DLPFC tDCS or sham during encoding, with free recall and recognition.
MCI randomised to tDCS or sham, with Wechsler Memory Scale outcomes.

Healthy men, M1 tDCS vs sham, with a pattern recognition memory task. Check the delay of the recognition test.
Healthy adults randomised to anodal or sham tDCS with retrieval practice, with a free recall test two days later.
Open-label studies with no sham condition.

Eyeblink conditioning, not an episodic-memory test.
MCI or mild AD, bifrontal, bitemporal and sham tDCS crossover, with ADAS-Cog word recall and word recognition.
